title: Lighting the First Torch
preview: An introduction to Descent Into Darkness, the studio's direction, and what 'dungeon extraction' means for this project.
body:
Welcome to the first entry in the Descent Into Darkness dev log. This is where the studio records the work as it happens — updates, patches, screenshots, and the occasional hard-won lesson from the dark.

What is Descent Into Darkness? It is an old-school dungeon crawler reforged for a modern audience: a grim underground fantasy of torchlit corridors, cursed ruins, and the relentless arithmetic of risk and reward. You assemble a party, descend into the dark, and decide with every room whether to press deeper toward greater spoils or extract before the dungeon claims everything you carry.

The current focus is the foundation — visual identity, the core dungeon loop, and the feel of moving through a hostile place. More to come as the torch burns lower.

title: First Look at the Depths
preview: Early environment captures and a first look at the visual identity taking shape in the dark.
body:
A short one. We've been blocking out the look of the early dungeon and putting the first creature renders through their paces. These are early — mesh tests and lighting studies rather than final in-game shots — but they set the tone: black iron, worn stone, and just enough torchlight to make the shadows worse.

You can see the current renders over on the Screenshots page. Real in-game captures will replace them as the build comes together.

title: Combat Feel Pass
preview: Notes on making grim fantasy combat deliberate, weighty, and dangerous rather than fast and forgiving.
body:
Combat in Descent Into Darkness should feel like a decision, not a reflex. This pass is about weight: telegraphed enemy threats, committed swings, and stamina that punishes panic. A single mistake should echo across the whole run.

Early goals for the combat loop:

  • Readable enemy wind-ups and clear threat tells
  • Deliberate attacks with real commitment and recovery
  • Resource pressure — stamina, torchlight, and health all matter
  • Positioning and party coordination over button-mashing

Still rough, but the bones are forming.
